transcript: Tonight I attended the first preview of Parade on Broadway, fresh from its run at encores last fall. I didn't see the production at encores, but I heard great things about it, and I can testify that they are all true. Going in, I didn't know much about the show other than it's about a Jewish man who's wrongly convicted of a murder, the scores by Jason Robert Brown, and that this production stars Ben Platt, Michaela Diamond. Although Ben Platt is undoubtedly the lead, the music in the show is pretty well dispersed across many different characters, and every single performer was amazing. Another thing I took away from the evening was just how unfortunately timely the show is, exemplified ironically, by people outside the theater prior to the performance, protesting the show. There were police present monitoring the situation, but it was nevertheless uncomfortable and pretty upsetting to see. And to me, it's a testament to the importance of the show, especially right now. And with that, another playbill for my collection.
